coverage.target: performance-design.md §5: one lookup composition (gateway → Identity → reveal_auth_subject → provider metadata read, 3 s ceiling in Identity's adapter, ≤1 s p95 share) with no partial render and `503` never a stored role; the 2 s p95 itself is measured by gateway/Identity service metrics (§8)

performance-design.md §2: optional `deadlineMs` (15 s) on the shared `request()` with AbortController and a typed DeadlineError, timer cleared on every exit; the five U10 calls pass it, other console calls unchanged; MSW delayed-handler test asserts the timeout surface

performance-design.md §4 + §3: mutation renders transition and 'This change is audited.' from its own 200 body, then a non-blocking lookup refetch; one attempt (`retry: false`); the re-read's failure never erases the confirmed change

performance-design.md §4: disable/restore issue the call only from Confirm, render the answered status + audited line, then re-read; `409`/`503` re-read before reporting; no request before confirmation (MSW assertion)

performance-design.md §3/§7: `usePendingGrants` one read per mount and after each approve/revoke (`invalidateQueries`), `staleTime: 0`, explicit `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`/`refetchInterval: false`; the 100-row p95 is a server target with no automated gate (§8)
performance-design.md §7: `GrantApprovalQueue` reused unchanged (approve/revoke one attempt, shared per-IP budget, shell `onGrantChanged`); U10 adds no budget and no retry to them

performance-design.md §3: the console's `retry: false` defaults for queries and mutations are inherited by every U10 hook; no hook sets retry or retryDelay; a failing MSW handler is called exactly once

performance-design.md §6: `parseProblem` parses `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP-date) into `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds`; the 429 renders as its own state with the seconds and issues no automatic second request

performance-design.md §3: both U10 queries set `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `refetchInterval: false` explicitly, because the console's query client leaves TanStack Query's default `true`; the MSW suite asserts a window focus event issues no second request

performance-design.md §3: the section's unmount effect calls `removeQueries({ queryKey: ["admin"] })`, dropping the lookup and the grant list in one prefix match; a later visit is a fresh provider read

security-design.md §7: role read at lookup time through `RoleReader::read_role` on the existing adapter (connect 1 s / total 3 s / one attempt), subject resolved by `reveal_auth_subject`, `Role::from_claim` mapping, provider failure → `503` and never a stored or cached value

security-design.md §1: every U10 data call is a /v1 gateway path via client.ts over TLS; the console's pre-existing Google Fonts load is recorded as an existing origin this unit adds nothing to; no CDN data, analytics or telemetry is added

security-design.md §1/§4/§5: reasons in the JSON body only, the looked-up address in the body of D-S1's POST lookup, no record field in a query string; the residual internal UUID in the mutation paths is recorded explicitly rather than hidden

security-design.md §4 (D-S1): the lookup becomes `POST /v1/admin/users/lookup` with `{"email"}` so no address reaches an edge log whose production configuration this repository does not define; alternatives (redaction with no owner, accepted exposure, header on a GET) rejected with reasons; the contract ripple is dependency 1 in §12

security-design.md §2: the section reuses the memory-only session and writes no storage API value (token, address, record, reason); the record lives only in the query cache, removed on unmount and cleared on 401/403/sign-out/expiry
security-design.md §2: no JWT decode or validation in the console; the session's role decides only whether the section is offered; every route is authorised again server-side from the forwarded token

security-design.md §3: all five paths declared `requires_admin: true` in the gateway table and re-checked in Identity from the forwarded JWT; no path is service-token-only and the browser never calls a service directly

security-design.md §3: `max_requests_per_minute: 20` on the role, disable and restore routes, set in the same `Route` declarations this unit adds or widens; the 5/min budget stays reserved for erasure
security-design.md §3: 60/min on the lookup and the pending-grant list, each bounded per token; the lookup is the one address-at-a-time enumeration path and carries its own budget
security-design.md §3/§6: per-token `check_route` keying with the per-IP budget underneath; the limiter's per-replica scope is stated as the honest bound; a `429` is its own non-retried state

security-design.md §5: the record renders display name, email + verified flag, internal id, role, status and timestamps only; no subject, hash, token, wallet address, credential, holding, balance or entitlement is requested or shown (the metadata boundary of spec §3.2)
security-design.md §5: reasons are never pre-filled, echoed, logged, telemetered or placed in a URL/header; the forms state the transition and that it is audited
security-design.md §5: error surfaces show status and correlation id only; `ProblemDetails.detail` is never rendered; no audit id is displayed
security-design.md §2: record, address and reason drafts are memory-only; `removeQueries(["admin"])` on unmount and the console's existing cache clear on 401/403/sign-out/grant expiry/revocation
security-design.md §5: React's default escaping; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in the section; server strings are never rendered as markup

security-design.md §5: the unit writes and reads no audit record; it states that a change is audited, shows no audit id and renders no retained personal data — the audit write is U2/U5's server-side record in C9

logical-components.md §5: four of the five paths reuse Identity's existing use cases and repositories; this unit adds one bounded read (`SupportGrantRepository::list_by_status`) under Identity's own role and DSN, with no schema and no privilege change — the requirement's wording is refined explicitly, not silently overridden
performance-design.md §4 + security-design.md §7: no optimistic cache write; every success re-reads and every `409`/`503` re-reads before rendering; the console never claims nothing changed

security-design.md §3: gating is presentational; a support session that opens `#admin-users` gets `403` on its first call, rendered as the not-an-administrator line with the correlation id, never an empty list or a silent failure
security-design.md §7: mutations target the internal user id from the server's record, never the session's Supabase user id; no id translation exists in the browser

security-design.md §9: labelled region with a visible h2, `aria-current="page"` from the shell nav, visible labels, per-field `aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid`, keyboard operation throughout, no motion-dependent interaction
security-design.md §9: the confirmation block focuses Confirm on open, traps Tab between Confirm and Cancel, cancels on Escape and returns focus to the opening action on cancel or completion
security-design.md §9: `RoleBadge` and `StatusBadge` render label + shape from the console's `StatusPresentation` vocabulary for all three roles and five statuses; Parchment Ledger tokens only
security-design.md §9: completion announced in `role="status" aria-live="polite"` without moving focus; failure is `role="alert"` carrying its text and correlation id
security-design.md §9 + performance-design.md §8: every rendered state in every U10 suite passes jest-axe; a state without an axe assertion is a review-time defect
security-design.md §10: `createdAt`/`updatedAt` through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the browser's locale; statuses and roles rendered as words from the §5.1 mapping, never raw enum values

security-design.md §10: the design records the English/Vietnamese half as deferred, not met — the console has no i18n module; this unit adds its copy the console's way and forks no second mechanism; owner is a console-wide i18n module (tech-stack T7)
security-design.md §10: `Intl` degrades to its default rather than an empty or malformed date; no raw timestamp or epoch value is ever rendered
